The base HP and HP-TES systems were modeled using an in-house Modelica library [81]. The base HP is a rooftop unit comprising two headered, louver-finned microchannel heat exchangers (MCHXs), a single-speed scroll compressor, and an electronic expansion valve (EXV). The HP-TES integration has three additional components: a brazed-plate heat exchanger (BPHX), a water pump, and a PCM-TES heat exchanger. HX Transient Models The system consists of three types of HXs, namely, MCHX, BPHX, and PCM-TES, each modeled using three control volumes (CVs) connected via HeatPorts from the Modelica [82]. Figure 31 illustrates the control volumes used for each heat Standard Library exchanger type, all of which use the tube wall CV. The tube wall combines the thermal masses of the wall and fins (if present) and solves the transient energy balance through the wall between the two corresponding CVs. Figure 31: Modelica HX model representations: (a) MCHXs, (b) BPHX, (c) PCM-TES HX The refrigerant CV, used in BPHX and MCHX, solves the transient mass and energy balances [81], [83], [84], with state variables Pressure (P) and Enthalpy (h). The refrigerant flow is assumed to be one-dimensional. Furthermore, the transient model neglects axial conduction along the tube and does not account for refrigerant maldistribution; thus, the heat transfer in each tube is assumed identical.
